fixes.explanation: Rulers sounds grand, baker, like somebody handed them a crown. But God calls Canaan “…the land where they lived as foreigners.” (Exodus 6:4) Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were the new folks in town, and the land was something God promised to give them. I think that makes the promise even sweeter.

Right, groaning. God says, “Furthermore, I have heard the groaning of the Israelites, whom the Egyptians are enslaving…” (Exodus 6:5) He also says He has remembered His covenant. I think it's a comfort that He names the very sound they were making, friend.

Battle would be a whole different worry, baker. Moses isn't sweating over swinging a sword. He says, “…I am unskilled in speech?” (Exodus 6:12) That's like being nervous about giving a toast and somebody hands you a helmet. His trouble is opening his mouth in front of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.

Close to the idea of Aaron helping, baker, but not who picks the words. God tells Moses to pass on everything He says to him (Exodus 6:29). Then God says Moses speaks all that He commands, and Aaron is the one who tells Pharaoh to let the Israelites go (Exodus 7:2). So Moses carries the message and Aaron is his prophet, his spokesman. Aaron doesn't get to edit the script.

Search sounds so gentle, friend, like checking every pocket for your keys. But God doesn't say that about Pharaoh, king of Egypt. He says He will harden Pharaoh's heart (Exodus 7:3). Nobody's patting down anything here. The word is harden.

I get why you'd think so, baker. More signs and wonders sounds like it should change a king's mind. But God tells Moses that Pharaoh will not listen to him, even as the signs and wonders multiply (Exodus 7:3-4). So the answer is false. God goes on to say He will lay His hand on Egypt and bring His people out by mighty acts of judgment.
